resources.string: Reads charge, range and gear from an OBD-II or CAN adapter, for cars whose head unit does not report them. Tarmac only reads: an OBD-II adapter gets standard read requests, and a CAN adapter is opened listen-only. Nothing is ever written to the car.
No paired Bluetooth devices. Pair the OBD-II adapter in Android’s Bluetooth settings first (the PIN is usually 1234 or 0000).
Allow Nearby devices so Tarmac can connect to the paired OBD-II adapter.
No USB serial adapter (CDC-ACM) is plugged in. Adapters with an FTDI, CH340 or CP210x chip are not supported yet.
A CAN adapter needs the car’s signal map (JSON) to know which frames carry charge, range and gear.
Without a map Tarmac reads the standard battery PID, which few electric cars answer. A map adds the car’s own PIDs, such as its state of charge or gear.
Paste the car’s JSON signal map
Charge and range for Apple Maps
Tells the iPhone the charge and range from the adapter, so Apple Maps can plan charging stops. Applies at the next connection.
When the car reports only its charge, Tarmac works out the range from this figure. Without a range the iPhone is not told about an electric car.
Adapter not found. Check that it is plugged in or paired and that the car is on.
Tarmac may not use the adapter yet.
The adapter did not answer. Is the ignition on?
This CAN adapter has no listen-only mode, so Tarmac does not open it.
